topics.title: Tax planning proposal deliverable boundaries
topics.trigger: A buyer receives a broad promise to reduce taxes but no list of completed work products.
topics.principle: Compare the written deliverables and excluded work before comparing headline fees. Advice, preparation and implementation can be separate engagements.
topics.example: One quote includes an annual planning meeting while another includes documented recommendations and quarterly follow-up.

topics.title: Tax advisory recurring fee comparison
topics.trigger: A monthly package lists access to advisers without defining recurring tasks.
topics.principle: Compare the services, cadence and fee triggers in writing. Frequent access and completed compliance work are different benefits.
topics.example: A buyer compares a lower monthly fee with a higher package that includes scheduled reviews and limited preparation services.

topics.title: Tax projection assumption transparency
topics.trigger: A proposal presents projected savings before the buyer provides complete financial information.
topics.principle: Treat projected benefits as assumption-dependent estimates. Ask what facts, baseline and implementation work support the comparison.
topics.example: A firm presents an estimated deduction while the client has not supplied basis, participation or household income details.

topics.title: Cost segregation quote methodology
topics.trigger: Two study providers offer different prices and descriptions of technical work.
topics.principle: Compare source reconciliation, methodology, scope and preparer coordination. A lower fee or larger estimated deduction does not independently establish a better report.
topics.example: One proposal emphasizes a site review while another relies on remote evidence and neither explains missing-record handling.

topics.title: Cost segregation audit support terms
topics.trigger: A provider advertises audit support without specifying the work included.
topics.principle: Distinguish answering report questions, supplying workpapers and representing a taxpayer. Confirm limits, duration and additional fees in the contract.
topics.example: An investor assumes that audit support includes handling an IRS examination, but the proposal only includes clarification of the study.

topics.title: Amended return engagement scope
topics.trigger: A buyer asks for a lookback review covering several years and entities.
topics.principle: Separate issue identification, preparation, filing and follow-up. Each year, entity and state can require distinct work and factual support.
topics.example: A planning proposal includes a prior-year review but the buyer assumes three amended returns are already included.

topics.title: Form 3115 coordination scope
topics.trigger: A study proposal mentions catch-up depreciation but does not identify the professional handling the tax procedure.
topics.principle: A cost segregation report and a tax method change filing are different deliverables. Ask the preparer to determine the applicable procedure and required work.
topics.example: An owner orders a study for an older rental and discovers that the report provider does not prepare the tax filing.

topics.title: Bookkeeping cleanup opening balances
topics.trigger: A buyer requests cleanup but the provider starts from unverified account balances.
topics.principle: Compare how opening balances, prior-year adjustments and missing evidence will be resolved. Reconciled cash accounts do not prove every balance-sheet account is correct.
topics.example: A new bookkeeper cleans transactions while old shareholder loans and fixed-asset balances remain unsupported.

topics.title: Payroll correction vendor responsibility
topics.trigger: A client needs historical payroll changes and several professionals are involved.
topics.principle: Identify who investigates, authorizes, files and verifies each correction. A tax adviser recommendation does not mean the payroll provider has implemented it.
topics.example: An owner changes payroll firms after learning that a prior W-2 omitted an owner health insurance reporting item.

topics.title: Retirement planning provider roles
topics.trigger: A proposal combines tax planning with discussion of retirement contributions.
topics.principle: Clarify the roles of the tax adviser, plan administrator and investment professional. A tax projection does not replace plan design or eligibility testing.
topics.example: A business owner expects a large contribution while the administrator has not reviewed the employee census.

topics.title: Multi-entity advisory quote coverage
topics.trigger: A buyer owns several operating and property entities but the quote states one advisory fee.
topics.principle: List each entity, owner and return separately. The number of legal entities, tax returns and planning issues may not be the same.
topics.example: A company group includes two disregarded LLCs, a partnership and an S corporation with different owners.

topics.title: State tax work exclusions
topics.trigger: A package describes federal tax strategy but the buyer operates across state lines.
topics.principle: Ask which state filings, elections and nexus questions are covered. Formation in one state does not settle obligations arising from actual activity elsewhere.
topics.example: A remote business is formed in one state but has workers and sales activity in several others.

topics.title: Implementation responsibility comparison
topics.trigger: Two advisory proposals include recommendations but assign follow-through differently.
topics.principle: Compare who completes each step and what proves completion. A checklist marked recommended is not the same as a filed election or corrected payroll record.
topics.example: An owner assumes the tax adviser coordinates payroll and bookkeeping changes, while the agreement assigns both to the client.

topics.title: Tax adviser response standards
topics.trigger: A buyer values responsiveness but proposals use broad terms such as priority support.
topics.principle: Compare the channel, hours, response target and escalation route. A response commitment may mean acknowledgement rather than a completed technical answer.
topics.example: A buyer expects same-day technical advice although the provider promises only prompt acknowledgement during business hours.

topics.title: Tax professional credential verification
topics.trigger: A buyer sees credentials and testimonials on a proposal or website.
topics.principle: Verify the actual professional and role through appropriate official sources. The credentials of one team member do not automatically identify who signs or reviews the client's work.
topics.example: A firm advertises a CPA-led team while the buyer cannot identify the person responsible for the proposed return review.

topics.title: Tax advisory refund and cancellation terms
topics.trigger: A buyer considers an engagement with staged fees and work already begun.
topics.principle: Read the cancellation, earned-fee and refund provisions before signing. A marketing assurance may be narrower than the contract.
topics.example: A client cancels after a discovery meeting and document review but before a written plan is delivered.

topics.title: Tax report ownership and portability
topics.trigger: A buyer wants to change firms without losing essential history and work products.
topics.principle: Compare access to final deliverables, source documents and exportable records. Portal access and rights to internal workpapers may differ.
topics.example: A buyer expects every planning worksheet to transfer to a new firm, but the agreement defines a smaller set of client deliverables.

topics.title: Tax planning and tax preparation separation
topics.trigger: A buyer wants advice and annual filing from one provider.
topics.principle: Determine which services are actually included and who reconciles recommendations to the return. A planning engagement can exist without a preparation engagement.
topics.example: A client receives entity advice in November but their separate preparer does not receive the implementation evidence.

topics.title: Tax adviser deadline readiness
topics.trigger: A buyer requests work close to a filing or transaction date.
topics.principle: Compare the required inputs, dependency dates and acceptance of responsibility. No provider can responsibly promise completion of unknown work without relevant facts.
topics.example: A client sends partial records shortly before a deadline and assumes a signed agreement guarantees immediate filing.

topics.title: Tax notice support package comparison
topics.trigger: A buyer expects ongoing support for notices after a return is filed.
topics.principle: Distinguish explanation of a notice, payment-credit reconciliation and formal representation. Confirm which return periods and types of notices are included.
topics.example: A client receives an agency notice and discovers that their annual package covers only the originally prepared return.
